# Preface {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-important}
## An AI-directed project, early in its development

Every chapter here was researched and written by Claude, an AI model, working
from the primary literature under human direction. No chapter has yet been read
by a subject expert.

The project is built so that the claims can be checked rather than taken on
trust. Each statement traces back to a record naming the paper it came from and
the lines it was read from, the bibliography is generated from those records,
and several automated checks run on every change. Those checks compare numbers
and wording. They cannot catch a sentence that says slightly more than its
source, and some have got through and been corrected after the fact.

Two limits on that traceability are worth knowing first. Forty-two of the
sources behind this book were read as abstracts rather than as full text, and
seventeen are preprints that have not been through review. Both sets are listed
by name in [`research/ALLOCATION.md`](https://github.com/brianjohnhaas/IsoformBiology/blob/main/research/ALLOCATION.md),
and the chapters that lean on them say so in their own first-draft notices.

Read this as a referenced starting point rather than as a reviewed secondary
source, and go to the cited paper before relying on anything. Corrections are
welcome as [issues](https://github.com/brianjohnhaas/IsoformBiology/issues).
:::

A gene is not a transcript, and most human genes produce several, sometimes
dozens, where the differences between them are often the biology. Which protein
domain is present, which cell type expresses which form, whether a transcript is
translated at all or routed to decay: these are isoform-level questions, and a
gene-level answer cannot reach them.

Yet most transcriptomic analysis still collapses this to one number per gene.
That collapse is sometimes justified and often simply inherited from a time when
nothing finer was measurable. This book is an argument, built from the primary
literature, that the finer resolution is where a great deal of the biology
lives.

It is organized as a book rather than a tool list because the case is
cumulative, and it is ordered by what each step licenses. Landmark examples
across the tree of life come first, then the measurement arc that made them
visible and the catalogues it produced, then what an isoform difference does to
the protein. Variation, disease and drug targets follow, because each of those
arguments depends on the measurement being trusted first.

::: {.callout-note}
## Status
All thirteen chapters are drafted, from research records built one paper at a
time.
The checks that run on every commit, and the things they cannot see, are listed
in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

Three glossary terms rest on no source found in this book's corpus and are
written on its own authority. They are marked in place, and they are the
entries most in need of a reader.
:::
